name: Hashubah
title: Descendant of King David
summary: Hashubah was a descendant of King David through the lineage of Zerubbabel, mentioned in the genealogical records of Chronicles. He is one of the royal descendants registered after the exile in Babylon and represents the continuity of the Davidic line at a time when the kingdom had ceased to exist.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in David's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Hashubah is listed as one of the sons of Shemaiah in the genealogy of David's descendants after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Part of the royal lineage
keyEvents.description: Hashubah belonged to the royal Davidic line, which was carefully recorded after the Babylonian captivity to preserve the inheritance and promises connected to David's house.

keyEvents.title: Descendants of Zerubbabel recorded
keyEvents.description: Through Zerubbabel, who led the Jews back from exile, the lineage continued. Hashubah was part of this important line that carried forward the messianic promise.

keyEvents.title: Preservation of David's line after the exile
keyEvents.description: After returning from Babylon, it became essential to document the Davidic lineage. Hashubah is part of this record, demonstrating God's faithfulness to the promises given to David.
